bucket: floating flower barges on a canal
brief: Flat-bottomed barges and punts moored or drifting on a still canal, loaded so heavily with cut blooms and potted plants that the boat itself nearly disappears under them. The water is the subject this pool always describes, so keep the canal itself central: its surface, its colour, what the flower-laden hulls do to the reflection. Vary the flowers (peonies, dahlias, lilies, tulips, chrysanthemums, hydrangeas), the barge (a long painted narrowboat, a low sampan, a wide raft of lashed planks, a rowboat brimming over), and the arrangement (a single barge mid-channel, a line of them nose to tail, two rafted together, one just cast off with a wake). Canals already exist in this pool; the BARGES are the new thing, so the boat and its cargo must be unmistakable in every entry. No people.

A cosy little railway journey. Vary the vantage: a plush compartment with the countryside streaming past the window, a corridor between carriages, a dining car with tiny cups sliding on the table, the open platform at the rear, a luggage rack turned into a nest, a window seat with a forehead against the glass. Vary the train itself (a brass-and-green steam locomotive, a wooden narrow-gauge carriage, a sleek pastel streamliner) and the land it crosses (meadow, viaduct over a gorge, tunnel mouth, snowy pass, coastline). Small cosy specifics do the work: ticket stubs, a folded map, a thermos, curtains swaying, a lamp bobbing. Keep the storybook warmth this pool always has.

A small passenger ferry working between two points of the aquatic village. Vary the moment: nosing into a floating jetty, mid-channel with both shores distant, ropes being cast off, loading at a ramp, arriving at dusk with lanterns lit, waiting at an empty landing in fog. Vary the vessel (a stubby wooden steam ferry, a broad flat punt on a hand-drawn cable, a many-oared longboat, a shell-hulled skiff) and the infrastructure (pilings, a gangplank, a bell on a post, a ticket hut on stilts, mooring rings). This pool describes SETTINGS, so build the whole crossing as a place: the water, the landings, the village behind. Submarine-ports and vessel-cottages already exist here; a working FERRY ROUTE is the new idea.

The inside of a small second-hand bookshop while it rains outside. Vary the corner: a window seat with a streaming pane, a reading nook wedged between shelves, a spiral stair between floors, a counter stacked with unsorted stock, a back room of crates, a landing where shelves meet a skylight drumming with rain. Specifics sell it: leaning towers of books, a ladder on a rail, a tipped-over stack, paper curling in the damp, a brass lamp, a dripping umbrella, a rug gone dark at the door, tea going cold on a shelf edge. Keep the rain present and audible-feeling in every entry, the way this pool always does.

Vary the vantage: a lane of striped awnings, a single trestle heaped with produce, the space between two stalls, a corner flower stand, a cheese-and-preserves table, the tail of a cart being unloaded, the square at the end of the day with crates stacking. Specifics: chalk price boards left blank, wicker baskets, scales, hand-lettered-looking tags with no readable text, bunched carrots, trays of eggs, jars of honey, a canvas canopy sagging with rain. Build it as a PLACE the way this pool always does, not as a single object, and keep the soft cottagecore warmth.

Vary the sky (a dozen tiny diamonds, one enormous fish-shaped banner, a chain of paper discs climbing, long ribbon tails crossing, a single kite far up in clear blue) and the ground (a grassy ridge, a wide beach at low tide, terraced fields, a river meadow, a clifftop). Specifics: line spools, tangled string, a kite down in the grass, bunting on poles, a picnic blanket weighted with stones, a windsock. Keep this pool's habit of describing a whole WORLD with distance and layers, not a close-up.

Specifics: tiered plates of buns, tarts under glass domes, a tin of coins, chequered cloth, a blank chalk board, a cake with a slice already out, paper cases, a jug of lemonade sweating in the heat, wasps circling. Keep the bright, open, sunlit register this pool always uses, and build it as a place in the village rather than a food close-up.

A small hilltop observatory at night, and the meadow around it. Vary the vantage: the dome with its shutter open and a telescope barrel angled out, the terrace beside it with a smaller scope on a tripod, an equipment table, the track up through long grass, the dome seen small against a huge sky, the inside of the dome with the sky through the slot. Specifics: a folding stool, a red-filtered lamp, star charts weighted against the breeze, a thermos, a blanket, dew on the instrument, moths at the lamp. Keep the night-meadow softness this pool has: the sky is enormous, the building is small and human-scaled.

A vast arid dune field in deep prehistory. Vary the form: long transverse ridges marching to the horizon, a single towering star dune, a wind-scoured corridor between dunes, a dune field spilling against bare rock, a dry pan between them cracked into plates, a slope avalanching in the wind. Specifics that make it PALEO rather than modern desert: wind-stunted cycads and low scrub in the hollows, a dry wash with petrified trunks, a scatter of bleached bone, fossil-bearing strata exposed at the margin, ripples printed sharp across every flank. Match this pool's habit of naming scale in feet, the light, and the ground texture, and keep it people-free.

High conifer forest in deep prehistory, right where the trees give out and the snow begins. Vary the form: a stand of tall araucaria thinning into bare rock, a ridge with snow in the lee of every trunk, a boulder field above the last trees, a hanging valley with a frozen tarn, a slope of wind-flagged timber, a pass with cloud pouring through it. Specifics: rime on needles, snow lying in the shadow side only, black wet rock, lichen, a melt stream cutting the snowpack, deadfall bridging a gully, breath-cold air. Keep this pool's scale cues and light description, and keep it people-free.

An old stone or timber bridge deep in the enchanted wood, so overgrown it is half landscape. Vary the structure: a single-arch stone span furred green, a flat slab clapper bridge over a brook, a rope-and-plank crossing swaying above a gorge, a fallen giant trunk worn into a path, a many-arched viaduct with trees rooted in its parapet, stepping stones with a broken arch beyond. Specifics: moss thick enough to hide the joints, ferns from the mortar, a worn hollow where feet have passed, water below, mist in the span, a handrail gone soft with rot. This is a VISTA pool, so give the whole view depth: the bridge, what it crosses, and the wood receding beyond it.

Specifics: whey in a channel on the floor, a wide shallow pan, cheesecloth in folds, a wooden paddle worn pale, chalk marks on a beam with no readable writing, brine crust on a barrel rim. Match this pool's voice exactly: it opens on one object doing its job at the centre of the room, then names the tools and surfaces around it, all of them showing use.

Match this pool's voice: one object at the centre doing its job, then the worn tools and surfaces around it.

The stable end of the barn early in the day, with horses as the SUBJECT rather than as props. A library built down into a catacomb, where the shelving and the ossuary are the same architecture. Vary the space: shelves fitted into burial niches, a barrel-vaulted corridor lined floor to ceiling with tomes, a rotunda with a reading table under a shaft of light, a spiral stair between stacked levels, a collapsed section where books have spilled, a cell-sized study cut into the rock. Specifics: chained volumes, ledgers swollen with damp, candle stubs welded to stone by their own wax, a lectern, iron grilles, skulls shelved among the bindings, dust, cold stone sweating. Match this pool's register exactly: long architectural sentences, deep recession, light arriving from far off and losing the fight.

A small boat on a still lake under the moon. Vary the arrangement: a rowboat adrift mid-water with its oars shipped, a punt among reeds, a boat pulled half out on a shingle bank, one tied at the end of a long jetty, a boat far out as a silhouette, a hull seen close with black water lapping. Specifics: the moon's track broken on the ripples, mist standing on the surface, a lantern at the bow, a rope trailing, water beaded on the gunwale, drowned trees, the far shore as a low black line. This pool has harbours and old boats already; a LAKE at NIGHT with the moon doing the lighting is the new idea. Keep the cold, still, unhurried gothic register.

A glasshouse given over entirely to near-black roses. Vary the space: a long nave of staging with blooms down both sides, a domed end with a single enormous climber, an aisle where canes have reached the glass and turned back, a propagation bench of cuttings, a corner where panes are gone and frost has got in, the exterior seen through fogged glass with the dark mass inside. Specifics: petals so deep red they read black, thorned canes thick as rope, a pruned heap on the floor, iron ribs, whitewash flaking, condensation running, frost on the outside of the panes and bloom on the inside. This pool already has derelict conservatories; the ROSES are the new subject, so they must dominate every entry.

Vary the vantage: looking up the flight with the torii framing the top, looking down from the landing over the rooftops, a turn in the steps under heavy trees, the stone lanterns along the edge, the washbasin at the top, a shaded rest halfway with the light hammering outside it. Specifics: heat shimmer, moss in the step joints, a discarded cicada shell on a rail, dropped leaves, a bright sky through the canopy, sweat-bright stone, an ema rack with blank tags, a bell rope. Match this pool's exact voice: it names foreground, midground and background in one breath and places the figure mid-action.
